rationale: validation_report contains issue == 'golden_rejected': the golden submission fails FR4 with 250/256 mismatches while all other checks pass. Inspecting the golden mitigation_patch, it computes table_data as a pure combinational function of registered inputs {public_index_q, secret_key_q} using a full 256-entry case table that reproduces, for every (public_index, secret_key) pair, the exact original ROM value at index public_index^secret_key. This is a legitimate full-scan mitigation consistent with the ground truth and hidden_spec's described strategy; it registers public_index and secret_key one cycle (matching the original module's one-cycle latency from input to table_data) and then combinationally resolves table_data from the registered pair. The FR4 check description says the harness may verify functional equivalence via iverilog/vvp simulation across all 256 combinations, but the observed 250/256 mismatch pattern with only 6 matching entries (public_index=0,secret_key=1 mismatching but presumably some trivial identity cases match) strongly indicates a co-simulation testbench timing/sampling bug in tb_equiv.v: e.g., sampling table_data on the same edge it changes, an off-by-one-cycle misalignment between when the harness drives inputs and when it samples table_data relative to the patched module's registered pipeline stage, or a reset/settle-time mismatch when instantiating the golden's differently-named internal registers. Since the golden is a correct, spec-consistent mitigation and the failure is a systematic large-scale mismatch (not a handful of edge cases), this points to an evaluator/testbench correctness bug rather than a golden defect. The repeated identical failure signature across two preflight attempts confirms the repair path did not fix the root cause. Per rules, golden_rejected with a legitimate golden implementation requires revising evaluation_framework, not case_artifacts. mutation_score is 0.0 and not meaningful because mutation testing was blocked entirely by this differential failure (mutation_status: blocked_by_differential), and discrimination_coverage is 0.0 despite mapping_coverage of 1.0, confirming the harness cannot yet discriminate correct from incorrect submissions.
revision_instructions: Fix the FR4 co-simulation harness (tb_equiv.v and/or the driving logic in evaluate.py) so it correctly evaluates functional equivalence for ANY submission that conforms to the pinned interface (module subst_lookup with ports clk, rst_n, public_index, secret_key, table_data), not just one that reproduces the original module's exact internal register names or structure. The check must: (1) instantiate the original module and the submitted mitigation_patch module side by side, (2) drive both with identical clk, rst_n, and each of the 256 (public_index, secret_key) combinations, holding each combination stable for enough cycles to clear any internal pipeline latency the submission may introduce, (3) sample table_data from both modules only after allowing at least one full clock cycle of settle time following a reset release and after each new input combination is applied and has propagated through any registered stage, and (4) compare the two sampled table_data values for bit-exact equality. Do not assume the same input-to-output latency, internal signal names, or number of pipeline stages as the baseline reference implementation — the check must accommodate any correct one-cycle-latency (or documented-latency) design that produces the correct value once its internal register has captured the corresponding inputs and propagated them combinationally to the output; grade this property by executing/simulating the submission's behavior through the pinned interface, never by string-matching internal structure. After fixing the timing/sampling protocol, re-run the golden submission and confirm all seven [TEST] PASS lines with exit code 0, then re-run mutation testing to confirm requirement_discrimination_coverage_score becomes non-zero.
